---
title: Loading, failing, and having no picture at all
version: 1
---

**An image on a screen has four states, and three of them are not the image.** It is loading; it
loaded; it failed, because the server answered `404` or the phone is offline; or there is nothing to
load, because the course has no cover. Each of the last three needs something drawn in its place,
and the wrong default is the one where the space collapses and the card jumps when the picture
arrives. `CourseCard` of section 02 gave each its painter: grey while loading, red on failure,
darker grey when the URL is `null`, always in the same 120 dp.

Waiting for a real network to be slow, or to fail, makes a bad test. **`coil-test` swaps the loader's
engine for a fake** that answers each URL with whatever the test decides, at once, so a screenshot of
every state is deterministic:

```kotlin
// app/src/test/java/com/example/planner/StatesScreenshotTest.kt
package com.example.planner

import android.content.Context
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Arrangement
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.Surface
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createComposeRule
import androidx.compose.ui.test.onRoot
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import androidx.test.core.app.ApplicationProvider
import coil3.ColorImage
import coil3.ImageLoader
import coil3.annotation.ExperimentalCoilApi
import coil3.request.ErrorResult
import coil3.test.FakeImageLoaderEngine
import com.example.planner.ui.CourseCard
import com.github.takahirom.roborazzi.captureRoboImage
import kotlinx.coroutines.awaitCancellation
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode

@OptIn(ExperimentalCoilApi::class)
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)
@Config(qualifiers = "w360dp-h860dp-xhdpi")
class StatesScreenshotTest {
    @get:Rule val rule = createComposeRule()

    @Test
    fun fourStates() {
        val context = ApplicationProvider.getApplicationContext<Context>()
        val engine = FakeImageLoaderEngine.Builder()
            .intercept("https://example.com/kotlin.png", ColorImage(0xFF3D5AFE.toInt()))
            .intercept({ it == "https://example.com/missing.png" }) { chain ->
                ErrorResult(null, chain.request, IllegalStateException("404"))
            }
            .intercept({ it == "https://example.com/slow.png" }) { awaitCancellation() }
            .build()
        val loader = ImageLoader.Builder(context).components { add(engine) }.build()
        coil3.SingletonImageLoader.setUnsafe(loader)

        rule.setContent {
            MaterialTheme {
                Surface {
                    Column(Modifier.padding(16.dp), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)) {
                        CourseCard("Kotlin, loaded", "https://example.com/kotlin.png")
                        CourseCard("Android Apps, still loading", "https://example.com/slow.png")
                        CourseCard("SQL Databases, failed", "https://example.com/missing.png")
                        CourseCard("Statistics, no cover", null)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        rule.onRoot().captureRoboImage("build/outputs/roborazzi/course-card-states.png")
    }
}
```

Roborazzi writes a PNG only when it is asked to record, and `recordRoborazziDebug` is the Gradle
task that asks; lesson 21 explains recording and verifying. The test ran, and left one file:

```
ana@vm:~/planner$ ./gradlew --console=plain recordRoborazziDebug --tests "*StatesScreenshotTest" 2>&1 | grep -E "PASSED|FAILED|^BUILD|^e: "
StatesScreenshotTest > fourStates PASSED
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 36s
ana@vm:~/planner$ ls -l app/build/outputs/roborazzi/
total 32
-rw-r--r-- 1 ana ana 31116 Oct 30 17:07 course-card-states.png
```

```schooling-figure
{"image": "data:image/png;base64,", "alt": "Four course cards, one above the other, each with a coloured strip 120 dp tall above the course name: a blue strip for Kotlin, loaded; a light grey strip for Android Apps, still loading; a red strip for SQL Databases, failed; a darker grey strip for Statistics, no cover. All four strips are the same height.", "caption": "The four states of CourseCard, rendered by a Roborazzi test with a fake image engine."}
```

From the top: a cover that loaded, drawn in its blue; one still loading, in the placeholder's light
grey; one that failed, in the error painter's red; and one with no cover at all, in the fallback's
darker grey. **All four cards are the same height**, because the strip is sized by its modifier and
not by the picture, so nothing below a card moves when a cover arrives.

**Colour alone is a weak signal, and these painters are only that.** A real app would put an icon on
the failed state, or a short line of text, so that somebody who cannot tell red from grey still
learns the picture did not load. Lesson 7's contrast rules apply to it like to any other part of the
screen.

`SingletonImageLoader.setUnsafe` replaces the app's loader for the test. The name says what it is:
there is one loader for the whole process, and a test that sets it affects every other test in that
process; that is acceptable here because every test of this lesson that uses the singleton sets it
first.
